decisions.rationale: Valid. main.py docstring rule 2 says the call "sets no connect or read timeout, so a hanging api hangs us too", but the call has no timeout argument and httpx 0.28.1 applies Timeout(timeout=5.0) (reconciler venv: inspect.signature(httpx.get) default = Timeout(timeout=5.0)); service-to-service-calls/artifact.md line 41 teaches "HTTPX has a five-second inactivity default that timeout=None turns off". README line 147 says "remove timeout=None", which the starter does not contain. Same defect as ops-sme-001. Acceptance: the starter call, its docstring and README troubleshooting describe the same timeout behaviour, and that behaviour matches the page (five-second default, or timeout=None if the draft is meant to hang). The fix is a grader or wording change and adds no learner time.

Valid. Reproduced by the reconciler on a copy of the lab at c959eefb with its own passing solution (27/27) and LAB_PROJECT: swapping the codes (TimeoutException -> 502, ConnectError -> 504) passes 27/27, and an "except httpx.RequestError -> 502" placed before "except httpx.TimeoutException -> 504" passes 27/27. issubclass(httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.RequestError) is True in httpx 0.28.1, so the 504 branch is unreachable. tests/lab.mjs lines 235-237 match each pattern anywhere in the file. Same defect as ops-sme-009. Acceptance: reviews-error-mapping fails when the timeout handler does not raise 504 in its own except body, when the refused-connection handler does not raise 502/503, or when a superclass handler (RequestError, TransportError, HTTPError, Exception) comes before the TimeoutException handler; the hint no longer steers learners to RequestError without the ordering rule. The fix is a grader or wording change and adds no learner time.

Valid. Same defect as ops-sme-004. Acceptance: ci-build-push passes only expressions that push for non-pull-request (or main/tag) runs and fails inverted or always-true forms with a message naming which runs would push. The fix is a grader or wording change and adds no learner time.

Valid. Reproduced by the reconciler on a copy of the lab at c959eefb with its own passing solution (27/27) and LAB_PROJECT: adding a step with env PW: ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD }} and run: echo "$PW" | base64 passes 27/27, because tests/lab.mjs line 312 only flags a run whose own text holds a literal "${{ secrets.". secrets-in-ci/artifact.md line 11 opens with exactly this base64 leak, and README line 118 recommends routing through env. Same defect as ops-sme-003. Acceptance: ci-no-secret-prints fails any step that writes a value bound to secrets.* (directly or through step, job or workflow env, including encoded forms such as base64) to the run log; output piped into docker login --password-stdin, as README line 118 teaches, still passes; the shipped debug step cannot survive by moving its secret into env. Valid. Reproduced by the reconciler on a copy of the lab at c959eefb with its own passing solution (27/27) and LAB_PROJECT: timeout = httpx.Timeout(3.0, connect=2.0) as an unused local passes 27/27; a comment "# later: timeout=httpx.Timeout(3.0, connect=2.0)" with no timeout on the call passes 27/27; timeout=3.0 on the call (a valid explicit limit for connect and read) fails "the outgoing api call sets explicit connect and read timeouts". Part (a) is the same defect as ops-sme-008(a). Acceptance: comments and docstrings are ignored; the rule passes only when the outgoing call (or its client) receives an explicit timeout that sets connect and read limits; either a plain number is accepted or the README states that an httpx.Timeout with a separate connect limit is required. The fix is a grader or wording change and adds no learner time.

Valid. Reproduced by the reconciler on a copy of the lab at c959eefb with its own passing solution (27/27) and LAB_PROJECT: {"authorization": authorization} and the guarded form (headers = {}; if authorization: headers["Authorization"] = authorization) both fail reviews-auth-forward, while a comment '# "Authorization": authorization' on a call with headers={} passes 27/27. In the reconciler's httpx 0.28.1 venv, a request with headers={"Authorization": None} raises TypeError "Header value must be str or bytes, not <class 'NoneType'>", which none of the taught except clauses catch, so the only accepted shape gives a 500 for a header-less caller (handler declares authorization: str | None = Header(default=None), main.py line 27). Same defect as ops-sme-010. Acceptance: comments are ignored; any form that forwards the incoming value as the outgoing Authorization header (either key case, dict literal or subscript) passes; a missing header no longer ends as an unhandled 500 in the form the README teaches (guard, 401, or required parameter), and the README says which. The fix is a grader or wording change and adds no learner time.

Valid, narrowed. starter/decisions.yaml: every store_contrast option list (lines 42-44) is ordered relational, document, key-value, matching the field order, so all 9 answers are positional; the first-listed option is also correct for shared_concern_at_gateway, compose_service_names_are, different_store_types_are_enabled_by, jenkinsfile_stages_run, keeps_three_replicas_running and manual_approval_before_production. Distractors image-caching, build-caching and a-container-registry are not taught alternatives for those questions. The options are slugs of sql-vs-nosql/artifact.md table cells (lines 15-17), and the brief's cart scenario (architecture-brief.md lines 52-53) and Approve scenario (lines 77-78) restate sql-vs-nosql line 11 and jenkins line 44. The reconciler's solution passes every why with 22 filler characters (tests/lab.mjs line 330). Binding: option order no longer predicts the answer in any section; each distractor is a plausible taught alternative; the scenarios differ from the pages' worked examples. Not binding: brute-force by rerun (inherent to any public choice test) and the request for a produced, checkable artefact per objective; the length-only why check is disclosed in the README (line 103) and stays. The finding is valid; the fix is a product decision. lab.json declares all 24 objectives, but these clauses have no executable task with a test: service-to-service-calls#o2 (Spring RestClient timeouts, and comparison with each client's default and with timeouts disabled: there is no RestClient file or comparison item); secrets-in-ci#o2 (add-mask and fork runs get no secrets: neither appears); jenkins#o2 (what a registry stores: only the reference split is tested). The terminology part of api-gateways#o2 (client-side vs server-side discovery) and the explain part of adding-fastapi#o3 (why 0.0.0.0: the task is the README-dictated swap of fastapi dev for fastapi run, README line 89) are elicited only weakly. The time budget is the constraint. The timing model (coding-lab-timing.json) gives typical 55 and worst 60 minutes and assumes the covered pages are already read. If the 799-word optional jenkins page that phase 7 depends on is charged to the lab (about 4 minutes at the model's 200 wpm, see ops-edu-12), the typical becomes about 59, which leaves about one retry at the model's 1 minute per retry. Phase 1 also allows 3 minutes for a 1139-word README (about 5.7 minutes at 200 wpm). Adding executable items for every missing clause therefore likely exceeds the 60-minute module-lab bound unless something is cut. Options for the owner: (a) undeclare the objectives whose clauses stay unelicited and record them as beta debt; (b) add small tested items (for example worksheet rows on HTTPX default vs timeout=None vs explicit limits, add-mask and fork secrets, client-side vs server-side naming, and what a registry stores), paid for by cutting tests 22 and 24 (the layer-order and .dockerignore repairs, which map to no declared objective and are image-layers-and-build-caching objectives o2-o3 of the previous module) and possibly test 21 (base image and WORKDIR), see ops-edu-18, and by trimming the README; (c) accept choice-only worksheet items as elicitation for the explain/compare objectives, as a recorded policy; (d) raise the bound. Reconciler recommendation: (b), with (a) for any clause that still does not fit inside 60 minutes, which keeps the lab inside the bound without declaring objectives from prose. Whatever the decision, the declared objectives must equal the set that tested tasks elicit. Operator decision (2026-11-18), verbatim: "Choose A. Keep all 24 objectives declared and required. Add the five small tested worksheet items, keep phase 7 required, state the S39 Jenkins reading as its prerequisite, and charge its approximately four minutes to S39. Fund the bound by prewiring the previous module's Dockerfile and .dockerignore work while keeping the CMD bind-address repair, and trim only redundant README prose. Re-prove that the typical path is about 55 minutes, worst case no more than 60, the starter fails exactly its declared tests, two independent private solved overlays pass, and no protected solution material enters Git or reports." The operator's "A" has the content of option (b) above (keep every objective declared, add small tested items, pay for them by cutting the previous module's image-build repairs and trimming the README), not option (a) above (undeclare); together with ops-edu-12 option (b) it keeps phase 7 required and fixes the bound. Decision changed from escalate to accept by ops-reconciler-r1 under that decision. Acceptance: all 24 objectives stay declared in lab.json and trackRequirement.standard stays required; the five small tested worksheet items are added for the clauses this finding names; phase 7 stays required with the S39 Jenkins reading stated as its prerequisite and its about four minutes charged to S39; the previous module's Dockerfile and .dockerignore work is prewired while the CMD bind-address repair stays a tested task; only redundant README prose is trimmed; the timing record re-proves a typical path of about 55 minutes and a worst case of no more than 60; the starter fails exactly its declared failingTests; two independent private solved overlays pass; and no protected solution material enters Git or reports. Elicitation residuals of the new items are tracked as ops-edu-r1-01, ops-edu-11 and ops-edu-03, and the no-protected-material residual in the solved-run record as ops-edu-r1-05, all in module-lab-recheck-reconciliation.json.

Valid, narrowed. README phases 4 and 6 give the exact decisive values: httpx.Timeout(3.0, connect=2.0) (line 97), HTTPException(status_code=504, ...) (line 98), needs: test (line 114), push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }} (line 117), contents: read (line 120). The ci-build-push failure message repeats the push expression (tests/lab.mjs line 280). For github-actions-pipeline#o2 ("Write a workflow ... using needs") the learner can copy the answer from the README, so the objective is not genuinely elicited. Same decision as ops-edu-10. Facts: lab.json trackRequirement.standard is "required"; topic.json and the calendar title S39's jenkins topic "Reading (optional): Jenkins, registries, CD and Kubernetes"; README lines 10-11 turn that page into a prerequisite for phase 7; test 20 (delivery: stage order, Deployment/Service, delivery vs deployment) is taught only on that page, and test 15's registry/repository/tag split is taught only there (the previous module only shows a full image name in passing, containers-and-compose/containers-and-images/artifact.md line 37); phase 7 budgets 4 minutes and the timing model does not count reading the 799-word page. There is no implementer-only fix that keeps jenkins o1-o3 declared, keeps the page optional and adds no time: copying the facts into the brief costs reading time and turns the items into lookup, and making phase 7 optional takes jenkins o1-o3 off the required path. Options: (a) make phase 7 (tests 15 and 20) an optional extension outside the required pass and record jenkins o1-o3 as beta debt for the required lab; (b) keep it required, count the page-reading time in the S39 estimate and make the README say plainly that Standard learners must read the page; (c) put the needed facts in the brief and accept lookup-level elicitation. The reconciler recommends (a), because the reading is labelled optional at programme level. Operator decision (2026-11-18), verbatim: "Choose A. Keep all 24 objectives declared and required. Add the five small tested worksheet items, keep phase 7 required, state the S39 Jenkins reading as its prerequisite, and charge its approximately four minutes to S39. Fund the bound by prewiring the previous module's Dockerfile and .dockerignore work while keeping the CMD bind-address repair, and trim only redundant README prose. Re-prove that the typical path is about 55 minutes, worst case no more than 60, the starter fails exactly its declared tests, two independent private solved overlays pass, and no protected solution material enters Git or reports." For this finding the decision has the content of option (b) above (keep phase 7 required, count the page-reading time in the S39 estimate, and have the README say plainly that Standard learners must read the page), not option (a) above (make phase 7 optional). Decision changed from escalate to accept by ops-reconciler-r1 under that decision. Acceptance: phase 7 and its tests stay on the required Standard path; the README states the "Reading (optional): Jenkins, registries, CD and Kubernetes" page as phase 7's prerequisite and tells Standard learners to read it; its about four minutes (799 words at the model's 200 wpm) are charged to S39 consistently in the README, coding-lab-timing.json and lab.json minutes.standard-s39; and the whole lab stays inside the operator's bound (typical about 55, worst no more than 60).

Valid, narrowed. Reproduced by the reconciler on a copy of the lab at c959eefb with its own passing solution (27/27) and LAB_PROJECT: a login with GITHUB_TOKEN and permissions {contents: read, packages: write} fails both ci-secret-refs (it requires secrets.REGISTRY_USERNAME/REGISTRY_PASSWORD) and ci-permissions ("no permission here needs write", tests/lab.mjs lines 323-324), while the lab pushes to ghcr.io. The secrets-in-ci page teaches both patterns: its terminal activity uses a REGISTRY_PASSWORD repository secret with contents: read only (artifact.md lines 63 and 100), and its MCQ keys D "contents: read and packages: write" for a GHCR push signed in with GITHUB_TOKEN and explains that C (contents: read only) is refused (artifact.html, a4 options). So the lab's message is false for the GITHUB_TOKEN route that the page itself keys as correct. Acceptance: for a ghcr.io push, the GITHUB_TOKEN + contents: read + packages: write route passes, or the lab targets a registry where a stored credential is needed and says why; failure messages are true for whichever route is shown. Page edits are not required by this decision. The fix is a grader or wording change and adds no learner time.
